## Objective
Identify duplicate sections of tissue in whole slide images and label the smallest for exclusion.

## Model
This is not a machine learning model, but an traditonal programming approach, involving four steps:
1) Simplifying the tissue polygons (makes the script run much faster)
2) Merge tissue polygons that are within a set distance to each other to a "fragment set"
3) Assign fragment sets that are above a certain similiarity score as duplicates (may also be triplicates, or quadruplicets)
4) Label the largest of the duplicate fragment sets for inclusion and others for exclusion

## Parameters:
- simplification_value: this is the size threshold under which feature details are removed 
- buffer_radius_um: (50% of the minimum distance between two tissue polygons to be considered as the same fragment set)
- similarity_threshold: fragment sets above this threshold are considered duplicates


## Tuning
Versions with different parameter settings are evaluated in 
the labl_2020_tuning set, based on detected errors parameter adjustments are made until satisfactory.

## Input
- image_names (a character vector of image names)
- image_metadata (a df with pixel size)
- file directory for input geojson (this script uses the output of the "tissue_vs_glass" model
- file directory for output geojson

## Output
- <image_name>_fragment_sets.geojson
- duplicates_<version>_metrics.xlsx
- similarity_duplicates_<version>.json (contains similarity and assessment for all fragment_sets)
- similarity_duplicates_<version>.tif(density by confidence for actual positives and negatives)


```{r libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

library(jsonlite)
library(nngeo) #remove holes in outline
options(scipen = 999) #turn of scientific notation
library(readxl)
library(writexl)

define_fragment_sets <- function(image_names, image_metadata, input_dir, output_dir, buffer_radius_um, 
                           simplification_value,  similarity_threshold) {
  
  # Loop through image names
  for (image_name in image_names) {
    
    print(paste0("Processing image ", image_name))
    
    # Metadata and parameter calculation
    metadata <- image_metadata %>% filter(name == image_name)
    buffer_radius_pixel <- buffer_radius_um / metadata$pixelSize
    
    # Read coordinate file
    coordinate_file_name <- paste0(image_name, "_tissue_1")
    coordinate_file_path <- paste0(input_dir, coordinate_file_name, ".geojson")
    
    tissue <-  st_read(
      coordinate_file_path,
      quiet = TRUE
    ) %>%
      st_set_crs(0) %>%
      st_make_valid() %>%
      st_remove_holes() %>%
      st_simplify(dTolerance = simplification_value)
    
    # Generate fragment sets
    fragment_sets <- st_buffer(tissue, dist = buffer_radius_pixel) %>%
      st_cast('POLYGON') %>%
      st_as_sf() %>%
      mutate(image_name = image_name,
             fragment_set_area_um2 = st_area(geometry) * metadata$pixelArea) %>%
      arrange(desc(fragment_set_area_um2)) %>%
      mutate(name = sprintf("%02d", row_number()),
             classification = "fragment_set") %>%
      select(image_name, name, classification, fragment_set_area_um2, geometry)
    
    
    # Check for duplicates (similar in size) and mark for include T/F based on size in duplicate set
    similarity_function <- function(a, b) {pmin(a, b) / pmax(a, b)}
    similarity_threshold <- similarity_threshold
    
    if (nrow(fragment_sets) < 2) {
      comparison_df <- data.frame(
        image_name = image_name,
        fragment_1 = fragment_sets$name[1],
        fragment_2 = NA,
        fragment_pair = NA,
        area1 = NA,
        area2 = NA,
        similarity = NA,
        duplicates = FALSE,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      
      fragment_sets <- fragment_sets %>%
      mutate(include = TRUE,
             classification = "include_set")
      
      } else {
        combos <- t(combn(seq_len(nrow(fragment_sets)), 2))
        comparison_df <- data.frame(
          fragment_1 = fragment_sets$name[combos[, 1]],
          fragment_2 = fragment_sets$name[combos[, 2]]
          ) %>%
          mutate(
            image_name = image_name,
            fragment_pair = paste0(fragment_1, "_vs_", fragment_2),
            area1 = fragment_sets$fragment_set_area_um2[match(fragment_1, fragment_sets$name)],
            area2 = fragment_sets$fragment_set_area_um2[match(fragment_2, fragment_sets$name)],
            similarity = similarity_function(area1, area2),
            duplicates = similarity >= similarity_threshold
      )
        
        # Create a data frame of fragments involved:
    fragments_in_compare <- comparison_df %>%
      # For fragment_1 side
      transmute(
        fragment = fragment_1,
        duplicates = duplicates,
        is_smaller_dup = ifelse(duplicates & area1 < area2, TRUE, FALSE)
      ) %>%
      bind_rows(
        # For fragment_2 side
        comparison_df %>%
          transmute(
            fragment = fragment_2,
            duplicates = duplicates,
            is_smaller_dup = ifelse(duplicates & area2 < area1, TRUE, FALSE)
          )
      )
    
    fragment_summary <- fragments_in_compare %>%
      group_by(fragment) %>%
      summarize(
        # Does this fragment appear in any duplicates?
        any_duplicates = any(duplicates, na.rm = TRUE),
        # Is the fragment ever the smaller one in a duplicate pair?
        any_smaller = any(is_smaller_dup, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(include = ifelse(any_smaller, FALSE, TRUE))
    
    fragment_sets <- fragment_sets %>%
      left_join(fragment_summary, by = c("name" = "fragment")) %>%
      # Fragments that never appeared in a duplicate comparison will have NA in include
      mutate(include = ifelse(is.na(include), TRUE, include)) %>%
      mutate(classification = ifelse(include, "include_set", "exclude_set"))
  }
    
    
    # Write fragments to GeoJSON
    file_name <- paste0(output_dir, image_name, "_fragment_sets.geojson")
    st_write(fragment_sets, file_name, driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
    
  }

  
  return(fragment_sets)
}

calculate_metrics <- function(df_assessed) {
  metrics <- df_assessed %>%
    summarise(
      TP = sum(duplicate_detection == "TP"),
      FP = sum(duplicate_detection == "FP"),
      FN = sum(duplicate_detection == "FN"),
      TN = sum(duplicate_detection == "TN")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      total = TP + FP + FN + TN,
      pct_positive = (TP + FN) / total * 100,
      pct_negative = (FP + TN) / total * 100,
      accuracy = (TP + TN) / total,
      sensitivity = ifelse((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), NA),
      specificity = ifelse((TN + FP) > 0, TN / (TN + FP), NA),
      ppv = ifelse((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), NA),
      npv = ifelse((TN + FN) > 0, TN / (TN + FN), NA)
    )
  
  return(metrics)
}


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

assess_similarity <- function(image_names, similarity_threshold, output_dir, df_assessed) {
  
  similarity_function <- function(a, b) {
    pmin(a, b) / pmax(a, b)
  }
  
  all_duplicate_checks <- data.frame(
    image_name = character(),
    fragment_pair = character(),
    area1 = numeric(),
    area2 = numeric(),
    similarity = numeric(),
    duplicate_prediction = logical(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (image_name in image_names) {
    
    # Read coordinate file
    fragment_set_file <- paste0(output_dir, image_name, "_fragment_sets.geojson")
    
    if (file.exists(fragment_set_file)) {
      fragment_set <- st_read(fragment_set_file, quiet = TRUE) %>%
        st_set_crs(0)
      
      # Only process if there are multiple fragments
      if (nrow(fragment_set) > 1) {
        
        combos <- t(combn(seq_len(nrow(fragment_set)), 2))
        
        comparison_df <- data.frame(
          idx1 = combos[, 1],
          idx2 = combos[, 2]
        ) %>%
          mutate(
            image_name = image_name,
            fragment_1 = fragment_set$name[idx1],
            fragment_2 = fragment_set$name[idx2],
            fragment_pair = paste0(idx1, "_vs_", idx2),
            area1 = fragment_set$fragment_set_area_um2[idx1],
            area2 = fragment_set$fragment_set_area_um2[idx2],
            similarity = similarity_function(area1, area2),
            duplicate_prediction = similarity >= similarity_threshold
          ) %>%
          select(image_name:duplicate_prediction)
        
      } else {
        # If only one fragment, create empty row with the same structure
        comparison_df <- data.frame(
          image_name = image_name,
          fragment_1 = NA,
          fragment_2 = NA,
          fragment_pair = NA,
          area1 = NA,
          area2 = NA,
          similarity = NA,
          duplicate_prediction = FALSE,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
      
      all_duplicate_checks <- rbind(all_duplicate_checks, comparison_df)
    }
  }
  
  # Add ground truth column
  df_assessed <- df_assessed %>%
    mutate(duplicate_ground_truth = case_when(
      duplicate_detection == "TP" ~ TRUE,
      duplicate_detection == "FN" ~ TRUE,
      duplicate_detection == "TN" ~ FALSE,
      duplicate_detection == "FP" ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ NA
    ))
  
  # Merge similarity results with assessed dataset
  confusion <- df_assessed %>%
    select(image_name, duplicate_detection)
  
  similarity_assessed <- left_join(all_duplicate_checks, confusion, by = "image_name")
  
  # Remove mismatched rows where duplicate detection and predictions don't align
  similarity_assessed <- similarity_assessed %>%
    filter(!(duplicate_detection == "TP" & duplicate_prediction == FALSE)) %>%
    filter(!(duplicate_detection == "FN" & duplicate_prediction == TRUE)) %>%
    filter(!(duplicate_detection == "TN" & duplicate_prediction == TRUE)) %>%
    filter(!(duplicate_detection == "FP" & duplicate_prediction == FALSE))
  
  # Categorize for plotting
  similarity_assessed <- similarity_assessed %>%
    mutate(Category = ifelse(duplicate_detection %in% c("TP", "FN"), "Is duplicate", "Is not duplicate"))
  
  # Create histogram plot
  bin_width_value <- 0.02  # Adjust bin width if needed
  
  plot <- ggplot(similarity_assessed, aes(x = similarity, fill = Category)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = bin_width_value, position = "identity",
                   aes(y = stat(density)), alpha = 0.5) +  # Density instead of count
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +  # Adjust x-axis breaks if needed
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Is duplicate" = "blue", "Is not duplicate" = "orange")) +
    labs(
      x = "Similarity",
      y = "Density",
      fill = "Category"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      axis.text = element_text(size = 9, family = "Arial"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, family = "Arial"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9, family = "Arial")
    )
  
  # Return both dataframe and plot
  return(list(similarity_assessed = similarity_assessed, plot = plot))
}

```



### duplicates_v1
First attempt with this type of input file (tissue_vs_glass).
Parameters are set using the values optimized for a similar approach 
(but with another input model and slide set <define_fragment_sets> < labl_2020_test>

#### Input
- <image_name>_tissue_1.geojson (output of model tissue_vs_glass_v2 (only class "tissue" used))
- duplicates_v1_assessed.xlsx (generated by assessing the fragment_sets generated by this script in qupath and documenting the results using the template from duplicates_v1_template.xlsx) - original here
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1DXYIrnMaYZZjpMh20Dd7Doz1EYFnxObprtnHerE_spw/edit?usp=sharing

#### Intermediate
- duplicates_v1_template.xlsx (template for assessment)

#### Output
- <image_name>_fragment_sets.geojson (duplicate_fragment_sets/output/labl_2020_tuning/duplicate_fragment_sets_v1/)
- similarity_duplicates_v1.json (contains similarity and assessment for all fragment_sets)
- similarity_duplicates_v1.tif(density by confidence for actual positives and negatives)

#### Assessment
- Errors that would be solved by decreasing the bufffer_radius:
    - The "FN" "9brj" have fragment_sets that are close together. Since only one fragment set is detected, this can't be solved by adjusting similarity threshold. Experimented with buffer radius for that a radius of 1725 would be the largest one that would solve it (1750 give false negative duplicates). 

- Errors that would be resolved by filtering out small tissue polygons before running this model (all
of this would also be solved by lower fragment_set buffers)
    - pxq6-0.46 
    - j0ei - 0.68
    - wkof - 0.73 

- Errors that would be solved by decreasing similarity threshold
  - ipx9 (0.67) - one fragment set is cutoff by the slide edge
  - qfw7 (0.72 - same as above)

```{r frag sets labl test, warning=FALSE}

tuning <- read_xlsx(paste0(to_box, "Projects/spatial/input/labl_2020_inclusion.xlsx")) %>%
  filter(pool == "tuning") 

image_names_tuning <- tuning$slideName[1]

image_metadata <- fromJSON(paste0(to_box, "Projects/spatial/input/image_metadata.json")) %>%
  mutate(pixelArea = pixelSizeUmX * pixelSizeUmY,
         pixelSize = round(pixelSizeUmX, 3))

input_dir <- (paste0(to_box, "Projects/fe_si_models/tissue_vs_glass/output/labl_2020_tuning/tissue_vs_glass_v2/"))

output_dir <- paste0(to_box, "Projects/fe_si_models/duplicates/output/labl_2020_tuning/duplicates_v1/")

assessment_dir <- paste0(to_box, "Projects/fe_si_models/duplicates/assessment/labl_2020_tuning/duplicates_v1/")

buffer_radius_um <- 2250

simplification_value <- 150

similarity_threshold <- 0.75

find_duplicates_run_time <- define_fragment_sets(
  image_names = image_names_tuning,
  image_metadata = image_metadata,
  input_dir = input_dir,
  output_dir = output_dir,
  buffer_radius_um =  buffer_radius_um,
  simplification_value = simplification_value,
  similarity_threshold = similarity_threshold
)

tuning_template <- tuning %>% select(slideName) %>% rename(image_name = slideName) %>%
  mutate(model_version = "fragment_sets_v1",
         buffer_radius_um = buffer_radius_um,
         simplification_value = simplification_value,
         similarity_threshold = similarity_threshold,
         duplicate_detection = "",
         comment = "")

write_xlsx(tuning_template, paste0(assesment_dir, "duplicates_v1_template.xlsx"))

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#Inspect the fragse the duplicates_v1_template and the fragment sets generated above in qupath,
#Grade them using the template (in google sheets), save as duplicates_v1_assessed and read back in
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
duplicates_v1_assessed <- read_xlsx(paste0(assessment_dir, "duplicates_v2_assessed.xlsx"))

#calculate performance metrics
duplicates_v1_metrics <-calculate_metrics(duplicates_v1_assessed)

write_xlsx(metrics, paste0(assessment_dir, "duplicates_v1_metrics.xlsx"))

#Assess similarity
similarity_assessed_duplicates_v1 <- assess_similarity(image_names_tuning, similarity_threshold, output_dir, duplicates_v1_assessed)

similarity_duplicates_v1 <- similarity_assessed_duplicates_v1$similarity_assessed

write_json(similarity_duplicates_v1, paste0(assessment_dir, "similarity_duplicates_v1.json"))
plot(similarity_assessed_duplicates_v1$plot)

output_path <- file.path(assessment_dir, "similiarity_duplicates_v1.tif")


# Save the plot as TIFF
ggsave(filename = output_path, plot = similarity_assessed_duplicates_v1$plot , 
       width = 7.08, height = 3.54, dpi = 300, 
       device = "tiff", units = "in")
```


### duplicate_fragment_set_v2
Adjusted buffer_radius from 2250 in v1 to 1725 (the highest threshold where the FN in 9brj is solved)

#### Input
- <image_name>_tissue_1.geojson (output of model tissue_vs_glass_v2 (only class "tissue" used))
- duplicates_v2_assessed.xlsx
#### Output
- <image_name>_fragment_sets.geojson (duplicates/output/labl_2020_tuning/duplicates_v2/)
- duplicates_v2_template.xlsx (template for assessment)
- similarity_duplicates_v2.json (contains similarity and assessment for all fragment_sets)
- similarity_duplicates_v2.tif(density by confidence for actual positives and negatives)
#### Assessment
Even though the stats are better for this then version 1, the problems detected are bigger.
- Errors that would be solved by increasing the buffer radius again
  -kz91 - this actually contains duplicates, but with these settings each fragment set is split again, and 3/4 fragments are excluded (loose both duplicates of one biopsy) - 1950 um is the lowest buffer that will solve this. Setting the buffer to that would inevitably lead to a FN in 9brj. I want to prioiritize not loosing fragments over keeping a duplicate, so should raise this back up. 
  - zhfu (0.75 & 0.87) - does not contain duplicates 
  
- Errors that would be solved by decreasing similarity threshold
  - ipx9 (0.67) - one fragment set is cutoff by the slide edge
  - qfw7 (0.70 - same as above)
  
#### Plan 
- Handle tissue fragments (filter small) before running duplicates
- Raise the radius buffer again (to at least 1950) (this will mean sacrificing "9brj") - other issues
- consider lowering significance threshold to 0.65
```{r frag sets labl test, warning=FALSE}

tuning_template <- tuning %>% select(slideName) %>% rename(image_name = slideName) %>%
  mutate(model_version = "fragment_sets_v1",

#calculate performance metrics
duplicates_v2_metrics <-calculate_metrics(duplicates_v2_assessed)

write_xlsx(metrics, paste0(assessment_dir, "duplicates_v2_metrics.xlsx"))
```
